liner.body_md:
## Setlist highlights

- **I Know Your Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 13 archived performances [15]
- **Cream Puff War**: rare: 12 archived performances [15]
- **Stealin'**: rare: 14 archived performances [15]
- **Your Sons and Daughters**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **Fire in the City**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-12-05.sbd.kimbro.23064.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 9 songs; 32 min; rated 4.4/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording runs 8% too fast; slowing it matches the tempo and keys of the November 1966 show [12]
- **gd1966-12-05.sbd.kimbro.21295.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 32 min; rated 3/5 by 5 [2]

## Around the show

- Listener asks about the vocalist and Warlocks connection in this early Dead recording [4]
- Recorded with jazz vocalist Jon Hendricks, who was hired to produce a movie soundtrack [5]
- Most tracks are January '67 outtakes; the track labeled Same Thing is actually King Bee [6]
- Jon Hendricks single is on YouTube; Warlocks uncredited but obvious, later re-released on Birth of the Dead [10]
- Songs were for opening and closing credits of a documentary about the Berkeley anti-war movement [13]
- Listener believes the instrumental is actually King Bee, noting the opening is very identifiable [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-12-05.sbd.kimbro.23064.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Teri Kimbro; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1966-12-05.sbd.kimbro.21295.sbefail.shnf**: source: sbd>mc>cass>cd [2]
